meta.subtitle: Reported growth runs well ahead of organic demand, a one-time tariff refund lifts margins, and the shares sit near their 52-week high.

advisories: model vs Street expected return diverge by 63pp — informational, not scored

analystSentiment.commentary: Coverage leans positive: of 16 analysts, 10 rate Zebra Buy, 6 Hold and none Sell, for a consensus Buy. The consensus target is $411.45, 11.9% above the current $367.54, with a median of $420.00 and a range of $350.00 to $455.00, so even the lowest target sits only a little below today's price. We are more cautious than the Street. Much of the second quarter's reported growth and margin came from an acquisition, currency and a one-time tariff refund, and consensus expects only modest EPS growth in FY27. We use the top of the Street's range as our Bull case rather than as a central estimate, and our scenarios, set out in the valuation section, derive HOLD.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Zebra Technologies Corporation describes itself as a global leader in the Automatic Identification and Data Capture ('AIDC') industry: mobile computing, data capture, RFID, thermal barcode printing and related workflow products, software and services. Founded in 1969 and headquartered in Lincolnshire, Illinois, it sells through a direct sales force and a network of channel partners to retail and e-commerce, manufacturing, transportation and logistics, healthcare, public sector and other customers. It reports two segments. Connected Frontline ('CF') covers mobile computing, point of sale, self-service kiosks and interactive touchscreen displays, workflow optimization software and related services. Asset Visibility & Automation ('AVA') covers thermal barcode printing and supplies, data capture, fixed industrial scanning, machine vision, RFID, real-time location systems and related services. On September 30, 2025 the company acquired Elo Holdings, Inc. ('Elo') for approximately $1.3 billion; the 10-Q excludes Elo from CF's organic growth, so the business sits in that segment. The fiscal year ends December 31, and the quarter covered here, ended July 4, 2026, is the company's second quarter of 2026.

thesis.label: HOLD
thesis.body: Zebra's second quarter, ended July 4, 2026, looks stronger than its underlying demand. Net sales rose {+ 20.4% +} to $1,557 million, but organic growth, which strips out currency and acquisitions, was 9.2%. Gross margin gained {+ 540 bps +}, which management attributes primarily to IEEPA tariff recoveries and favorable currency; the recovery is a one-time benefit of about $73 million, most of it not yet received in cash at quarter end. At $367.54, near the top of a 52-week range of $199.05 to $386.23, the shares trade at 17.5x this year's consensus earnings. We judge that multiple fair for the organic growth the company is showing, and our scenarios derive HOLD.

catalysts: Raised outlook: the August 4, 2026 release raised full-year guidance; the growth section sets out the ranges.
Organic momentum: second-quarter organic growth outpaced the opening quarter's, and AVA grew faster organically than CF.
Cash generation: management guides full-year free cash flow above $1 billion, which funds buybacks and debt service.
Restructuring savings: the substantially completed 2025 Productivity Plan is expected to deliver annualized cost savings.
Automation demand: management ties its outlook to trends in automation and Physical AI.
risks: One-time margin support: the tariff recovery does not repeat, and the third-quarter guide already points to a lower adjusted EBITDA margin.
Inorganic growth: a large share of guided full-year growth comes from acquisitions, dispositions and currency, and the boost from Elo ends once the deal has been owned for twelve months.
Cyclicality: Zebra's revenue fell sharply in FY23, and a repeat would take earnings well below consensus.
Leverage and liquidity: total debt has risen since the FY25 year-end and the current ratio sits below one.
Valuation: near its 52-week high, the share price leaves little room for a miss.

income.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.incomeCommentary: In the second quarter, ended July 4, 2026, net sales were $1,557 million against $1,293 million a year earlier, with growth in both segments and, in management's words, improved demand in all regions. The page's vendor rows label this quarter Q3'26 and show revenue growth of +18.0%; we use the filing's 20.4% throughout. Tangible products drove the gain at $1,316 million, {+ up 24.7% +}, while services and software grew 1.3% to $241 million. Excluding currency, acquisitions and dispositions, organic growth was 9.2% in the quarter and 6.8% for the six months, so the second quarter ran faster than the opening quarter. Gross margin rose to 53.0% from 47.6%, which management attributes primarily to the IEEPA tariff recoveries and favorable currency; it adds that price realization fully offset higher memory costs. Adjusted gross margin rose by the same 540 bps, so the non-GAAP measures appear to keep the recovery in. Operating expenses rose to $504 million from $433 million, mainly because of Elo, including intangible amortization, and higher employee-related costs, by the company's account; as a share of sales they fell to 32.4% from 33.5%. Operating income rose {+ 75.4% +} to $321 million, and diluted EPS was $4.85 against $2.19; non-GAAP EPS was $6.35 against $3.61. The annual record is why we discount the quarter: revenue growth was {- -20.7% -} in FY23 and diluted EPS fell to $5.72, before FY25 revenue of $5.4B, up 8.3%, and diluted EPS of $8.18.

balance.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.balanceCommentary: At July 4, 2026, Zebra held cash and cash equivalents of $157 million against total debt of $2,776 million. At the FY25 year-end debt was $2.5B and net debt $2.4B, against total equity of $3.6B. The filings give no reason for this year's rise in debt; over the same half, buybacks ran ahead of free cash flow (see cash flow), and management notes higher interest expense on higher average debt balances. The page leaves TTM net debt/EBITDA and interest coverage blank, so we do not size the leverage against earnings. Liquidity is thin: the trailing current ratio is 0.52 against 0.97 at the FY25 year-end, and it was below one in three of the last five fiscal years. We judge the balance sheet serviceable while free cash flow holds near guided levels, but it is the weak point if demand turns.

cashflow.note: Source: Bigdata.com company tearsheet (FMP); fiscal years ended December 31.

financials.cashflowCommentary: Cash generation supports the equity story. In the first six months of 2026, operating cash flow was $387 million and capital expenditure $26 million, leaving free cash flow of $361 million, while the company repurchased $568 million of stock. FY25 free cash flow was $831M, a 15.4% margin, and capital spending has been small in every year shown. Management expects full-year 2026 free cash flow above $1 billion. Two cautions temper that. Buybacks at the year-to-date pace would need cash from later in the year or more borrowing, since they exceeded free cash flow. And the cash line has broken before: FY23 operating cash flow was about nil and the FCF margin was {- -2.0% -}. We treat the guided figure as achievable on current demand, not as a floor.

multiples.note: Peer multiples pending a peer data source.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: The page shows a trailing P/E of 33.6x, a TTM EV/EBITDA of 17.4x, a P/S of 3.0x, and forward P/Es of 17.5x (labelled NTM) and about 16.6x on FY27E. The NTM figure equals the current price over the FY26E consensus EPS of $21.04, so we treat it as this year's multiple and use it as the like-for-like reference. The gap to the trailing multiple is partly basis and partly growth. The trailing figure is GAAP over the last four reported quarters, not FY25; the FY26E consensus sits inside the company's non-GAAP EPS guide (see Growth), so we read it as non-GAAP; and second-quarter non-GAAP EPS ran well above GAAP (see Financials). Two points weigh against this year's multiple. FY26 earnings include the one-time tariff recovery, which the non-GAAP measures appear to keep, so the multiple on recurring earnings is somewhat higher than it looks. And the shares have risen from a 52-week low of $199.05 to near the high. In its favor, the TTM FCF yield of 5.2% and the guided free cash flow (see cash flow) give the multiple cash support. The page has no peer multiples and no history of Zebra's own multiple, so we cannot call this year's multiple a premium or a discount to anything; we judge it fair for the organic growth on show.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Organic growth holds at or above the second quarter's pace, Elo delivers the growth and cost synergies the company is seeking, and margins hold up as the tariff recovery laps. Anchor: the top of the Street's target range, $455.00, which we take as the value a market paying for sustained growth could reach a year out.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Zebra delivers roughly its raised guidance, the tariff recovery does not repeat, and FY27 EPS reaches the $22.20 consensus. The market keeps paying today's current-year multiple of 17.5x on that year-ahead figure, giving $388.50: today's anchor plus one year of consensus growth, argued from both sides in the commentary.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Organic demand stalls as customers hold back hardware spending, the recovery is not replaced, and FY27 EPS stays at the low end of this year's non-GAAP guide, $20.75, instead of reaching consensus. The multiple falls to 13x, an assumed level we set below the 16.6x the page shows on FY27E because this case removes the growth that multiple pays for; 13x on that EPS gives $269.75. A full repeat of FY23 would go deeper; we treat it as a tail.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
We weight the scenarios 25% Bull, 50% Base and 25% Bear, for a weighted fair value of $375.44, expected upside of +2.2%, bear-case downside of -26.6% and reward/risk of 0.08×. The label derives HOLD.

The Base multiple is the main judgment, argued in the multiples commentary: cash support on one side, a year that includes a one-time gain and a price near its high on the other. We hold this year's multiple a year out, but the anchor does not decide the label. A Base at the Street's consensus target of $411.45 still derives HOLD, and so does a Base at the page's FY27E multiple, which equals today's price. SELL would need a Base multiple well below that FY27E multiple, and BUY a Base above the top of the Street's range.

The weights rest on each case's own evidence. The Bull weight rests on the second quarter's organic acceleration, AVA's faster organic growth and the raised outlook. The Bear weight rests on the third-quarter guide for a lower adjusted EBITDA margin (see Growth), a FY27 consensus that already shows only modest EPS growth, leaving little cushion before a stall, and the FY2025 Form 10-K's warning that Elo may not deliver its expected synergies. We see neither side as more likely. Moving ten points of weight from Bear to Bull, or from Bull to Bear, keeps the label at HOLD.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: The pack's segment table shows one consolidated line, but the 10-Q reports two segments; we follow the 10-Q. In the second quarter, Connected Frontline net sales were $903 million, {+ up 25.9% +} from $717 million, which the company puts down mainly to Elo, higher mobile-computer sales and currency; organic growth was 7.5%. CF gross margin rose to 51.2% from 47.3% on tariff recoveries and currency, partly offset by unfavorable business mix. Asset Visibility & Automation net sales were $654 million against $576 million, with organic growth of 11.4%, the faster of the two segments. By region, North America contributed $774 million, {+ up 21.3% +}, and Asia-Pacific grew {+ 23.1% +}.

moatFactors.name: Portfolio breadth and scale
moatFactors.body: Zebra describes itself as a global leader in AIDC and sells hardware, supplies, software and services across retail, logistics, manufacturing and healthcare. Research and development of $159 million in the quarter, 10.2% of net sales, funds that breadth. The pack carries no market-share data, so the leadership claim is the company's own.

moatFactors.name: Workflow embedding
moatFactors.body: The company says its products help customers digitize and automate workflows from factory production to the hospital patient journey. In our judgment that makes switching vendors costly mid-deployment. The recurring part of the relationship, services and software, barely grew in the quarter, so the attachment is not yet showing up as faster recurring revenue.

moatFactors.name: Channel and supplies
moatFactors.body: Sales run through a direct sales force and a network of channel partners, and consumables such as labels, ribbons and RFID tags are sold alongside the printers. We think that pull-through is harder for a rival to displace than a single hardware bid, but the pack gives no supplies revenue to test it, and it did not prevent the FY23 revenue decline.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat narrow. Breadth, workflow embedding and the channel give the franchise staying power, but the numbers show little protection: revenue fell sharply in FY23, and the operating margin was 13.0% in FY25 against 17.4% in FY21. By management's own account, this year's margin gain rests on the tariff recovery and currency, although price realization did offset higher memory costs, which is some evidence of pricing power. Durability depends on Zebra turning automation demand into organic growth above this year's rate. We would revisit the rating if that showed up in faster services and software growth.

points: Full-year 2026 guidance, raised on August 4, 2026, calls for sales growth of 14% to 16%, including about 8 points from acquisitions, dispositions and currency, an adjusted EBITDA margin of 23.5% to 24.0% and non-GAAP EPS of $20.75 to $21.25. The FY26E consensus sits inside that EPS range.

Third-quarter guidance calls for sales growth of 17% to 20%, including about 10.5 points from acquisitions, dispositions and currency, an adjusted EBITDA margin of about 22% and non-GAAP EPS of $4.70 to $4.90. That margin is well below the second quarter's 27.7%, which included the tariff recovery; the release does not explain the step-down.

Elo stops lifting reported growth once it passes twelve months after its September 30, 2025 acquisition date, when the 10-Q's organic measure stops excluding it, so the acquisition gap between reported and organic growth should narrow.

Consensus expects FY27 revenue of $6.6B against $6.2B for FY26, with EPS only modestly higher (see Valuation). We read that as a year in which the one-time recovery no longer adds to earnings; no source gives the Street's reasons.
The 2025 Productivity Plan is substantially complete, with cumulative one-time charges of $37 million and expected net annualized pre-tax savings of about $35 million.
Management ties its outlook to automation and Physical AI and cites progress on productivity and memory supply; the pack gives no figures for either, so we treat them as direction, not evidence.

management.leadership: William Burns is Chief Executive Officer and Nathan Winters is Chief Financial Officer; both are quoted in the August 4, 2026 earnings release. The 2026 proxy statement, dated April 3, 2026, lists the other 2025 named executive officers as Richard Hudson, Chief Revenue Officer, and Cristen Kogl, Chief Legal Officer, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary. Two named officers left their roles around the end of 2025: Joseph White, former Chief Product and Solutions Officer, resigned in November 2025, and Jeffrey Schmitz stepped down as Chief People Officer effective December 31, 2025 to serve as Senior Advisor to the CEO until a retirement the proxy planned for May 2026. The excerpt names no successors, so we cannot judge the depth of the team behind the top two.
management.capitalAllocation: Capital goes to buybacks and acquisitions; Zebra pays no dividend. Repurchases were $587M in FY25 and continued at a faster pace in the six months to July 4, 2026 (see cash flow), and the Elo purchase was the main recent outlay. The CFO calls this a balanced approach that lets Zebra invest for growth while returning cash. We read the year to date as more aggressive than balanced: buybacks exceeded free cash flow while total debt rose, and repurchases near the 52-week high buy fewer shares per dollar than those made lower in the range. The FY2025 Form 10-K, filed in February 2026, also notes that acquisitions could dilute stockholder value. Per the proxy, the annual cash incentive now weights adjusted EBITDA and net sales at 40% each, which ties much of annual pay to scale and profit.
management.governance: Per the 2026 proxy, the Board determined in February 2026 that every director was independent under Nasdaq rules except Chair Anders Gustafsson, Zebra's former CEO, and CEO William Burns. Mr. Gustafsson has been Chair since 2024 after serving as Executive Chair from 2023 to 2024. Because the Chair is not independent, the independent directors appoint a Lead Independent Director: Michael Smith, in that role since 2024, a director since 1991 and independent Chair from 2007 to 2023. Say-on-pay drew 94.2% support in 2025, and late-2025 outreach reached holders of 58% of the stock. A clawback policy has applied to Section 16 officers since March 2020. We see no governance flag in the excerpt, though a former CEO as Chair leaves the independent check concentrated in one long-serving lead director.
management.insiderOwnership: The proxy excerpt in the pack carries no beneficial-ownership table, so we make no claim about insider stakes. The securities-trading policy bars directors and executive officers from hedging, short sales, margin accounts and pledging Zebra stock as collateral.

idiosyncratic: One-time margin support: the second quarter's gross-margin gain rested primarily on about $73 million of expected IEEPA tariff refunds, of which $14 million had been received in cash, and on favorable currency. The rest of the refund depends on the U.S. Customs and Border Protection process, and the benefit will not recur.

Integration and impairment: the FY2025 Form 10-K warns that Zebra may not integrate Elo or realize the expected growth and cost synergies, and that the added goodwill and intangibles could become impaired. The deal represented approximately 9% of Zebra's market capitalization when it closed.
Cyclicality: FY23 shows how quickly the business can contract (see Financials). A repeat is the tail outside our Bear case, and it would take earnings well below the FY27 consensus.

Liquidity and debt: with a current ratio below one and debt rising this year (see Financials), a downturn would leave less room to keep buying back stock. The earnings release itself says that, because of its debt, interest rates and financial market conditions may adversely affect results.
Growth mix: once Elo laps, reported growth would slow toward the organic rate even if demand holds, which could disappoint a market that has priced the headline.
risks.systemic: Zebra is exposed to the broad enterprise spending cycle, and demand across retail, logistics, manufacturing and healthcare moves with economic activity. As a global company that relies on contract manufacturing and a global supply chain, it is sensitive to currency swings, tariffs and trade policy; the same IEEPA tariffs that produced this quarter's expected refund created the original cost. Component costs matter too, including memory, which management says it offset through price realization. The FY2025 Form 10-K names the war between Russia and Ukraine, conflicts in the Middle East region and the risk of increased tensions between China and Taiwan as geopolitical risks that could limit sales, and inflation as a source of higher costs and reduced or cancelled orders. None of these is unique to Zebra, but each can move a hardware-led business with thin liquidity.

body: We rate Zebra HOLD with a target range of $340 to $395. The second quarter was strong on paper, but the tariff recovery, currency and Elo carry much of it, and organic growth is well below the reported rate. At today's multiple, near the 52-week high, the price already reflects the raised outlook. Our weighted fair value of $375.44 implies expected upside of +2.2%.

On these scenarios the label would move to BUY at or below our target low and to SELL just above our target high. The scenarios themselves would change on evidence: signs that FY27 earnings will stall at this year's level would raise the Bear weight, and second-half organic growth at or above the second quarter's pace without the tariff recovery would raise the Bull weight.
